_readme: Every numeric quality floor in ITS lives HERE and nowhere else. scripts/check_quality_ratchet.py enforces it as a blocking CI step, and .github/workflows/ci.yml reads the coverage floor FROM this file rather than holding its own copy — two copies of a floor is a floor that drifts. Keys beginning with _ are prose (JSON has no comments) and are ignored by the checker.
_rule: A floor may be RAISED and a ceiling LOWERED by any PR, with no ceremony at all. Moving one the other way requires the entry to carry regression_reason + tech_debt_ref + expires (ISO date) — all three. The checker fails on a partial relaxation, fails once expires passes, and fails on a wrong-way move detected against origin/main that carries no declaration.
_why: Audit 2026-08-16. The finding was not that any one control was wrong; it was that six slope-controls had each been individually, reasonably relaxed, and the aggregate was a safety story that was narrated rather than enforced (Op Stds 52). A threshold that can be lowered under pressure will be, and every lowering will be locally defensible. What breaks that loop is not better judgment — it is an expiry that re-arms the control by itself.
_values: Set from measurement, never aspiration. Integer metrics sit at the EXACT measured value: one more CC>30 function, one more doc-convention warning, one more excluded verify check is precisely the event worth catching. The two float metrics sit at the measured value rounded UP to the next 0.001 — they are deterministic, so that is a one-notch tolerance rather than slack, and it keeps a single added branch from failing CI on the fourth decimal. Baselines on 14f38a1: erosion 0.38877, verbosity 0.06634, cc30 19, doc warnings 89, mypy 0, excluded verify checks 8, coverage 84.95% (CI-measured; the floor rounds down).
